title: missing lbEndpoint for second cluster in istio egressgateway proxy
body:
### Is this the right place to submit this?

- [X] This is not a security vulnerability or a crashing bug
- [X] This is not a question about how to use Istio

### Bug Description

Missing lbEndpoint for second cluster in istio egressgateway proxy 

STEPS:

- BringUp two k8s cluster and install 1.20.4 istio on the both
- Deployed say shopping in cluster1 which will connect to catalog service that is running in cluster2
- Configured the needed service entries, destinationrules and gateways 

**Service Entry:**

```
% k get se -n default        nsxsm.catalog  -o yaml
apiVersion: <redacted-host>/v1beta1
kind: ServiceEntry
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: "2024-03-21T09:12:41Z"
  generation: 1
  labels:
    cluster: eekkss
    createdby: test
  name: nsxsm.catalog
  namespace: default
  resourceVersion: "5908383"
  uid: 91b0df7f-0efd-4f18-be0d-b1ef76fede05
spec:
  addresses:
  - XXX.XXX.XXX.XXX
  endpoints:
  - address: istio-egressgateway.istio-system
    ports:
      http-catalog: 443
    weight: 1
  exportTo:
  - .
  hosts:
  - <redacted-host>
  location: MESH_INTERNAL
  ports:
  - name: http-catalog
    number: 8082
    protocol: HTTP
  resolution: DNS

```

**Destination Rule:**
```
% k get dr -n istio-system   <redacted-host> -o yaml
apiVersion: <redacted-host>/v1beta1
kind: DestinationRule
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: "2024-03-21T10:31:21Z"
  generation: 1
  labels:
    createdby: test
  name: <redacted-host>
  namespace: istio-system
  resourceVersion: "5928249"
  uid: 83ce0e72-16b0-461f-8f5a-d3e880e546a3
spec:
  host: '*.acme.com'
  trafficPolicy:
    loadBalancer:
      localityLbSetting:
        enabled: false
      simple: ROUND_ROBIN
    outlierDetection:
      baseEjectionTime: 120s
      consecutive5xxErrors: 1
      consecutiveGatewayErrors: 1
      interval: 1s
      maxEjectionPercent: 1
      minHealthPercent: 1
    tls:
      mode: ISTIO_MUTUAL

`

**gateway : Egressgateway**

`
% k get gw -n istio-system   istio-egressgateway  -o yaml
apiVersion: <redacted-host>/v1beta1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: "2024-03-21T11:36:53Z"
  generation: 1
  labels:
    app: gateways
    createdby: allspark
    release: istio
  name: istio-egressgateway
  namespace: istio-system
  resourceVersion: "5944911"
  uid: 4e1b90e3-09e5-4c94-aee4-68c96220440a
spec:
  selector:
    app: istio-egressgateway
    istio: egressgateway
  servers:
  - hosts:
    - '*.acme.com'
    port:
      name: tls-multicluster-listener
      number: 443
      protocol: TLS
    tls:
      mode: AUTO_PASSTHROUGH
```
**Expected:**

The shopping service in cluster1 should able to connect to catalog service in cluster2

**Actual:**
Receiving 503 error in shopping when tries to connect to catalog. **Same config worked with istio 1.19.3**

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant1 In my case the MTLS is enabled cluster wide. Please verify the configs below,

**Peerauthentication :**

```
% k get pa -n istio-system   default -o yaml
....
spec:
  mtls:
    mode: STRICT
```
   
**Destination Rule in istio-system for that domain:**

```
 % k get dr -n istio-system   mydr -o yaml 
....
    tls:
      mode: ISTIO_MUTUAL
```

**EgressGateway GW:**

```
k -n istio-system get gw istio-egressgateway  -o yaml
.....
    tls:
      mode: AUTO_PASSTHROUGH
```

So If I understand correctly In istio 1.20, setting "AUTO_PASSTHROUGH" not allowed in GW for cross clustering.

Adding following label to the service entry (spec.endpoints.lables) in istio-system namespace fixed our issue.

labels:
      <redacted-host>/tlsMode: istio
